Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 42, verse 35:

If you ask: what are the possible readings of the three forms of "wa-yaʿlama" (وَيَعْلَمَ)? I answer: as for the jussive (jazm), it rests on the apparent sense of coordination (ʿatf); as for the nominative (rafʿ), it is on the basis of a new resumptive clause (istiʾnaf). As for the accusative (naṣb), it is by coordination with a causal clause (taʿlil) that is implied, its estimated form being: "so that He may take vengeance upon them, and that He may know those who dispute..." and the like. Coordination upon an implied causal clause is not rare in the Qur'an. Among its examples is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that We may make him a sign for the people﴾, and His saying: ﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned﴾.

As for the statement of al-Zajjaj: the accusative is by the implied "an" (idmar an), because before it there is a conditional (jaza'), you say: "Whatever you do, I do the like of it, and I honour you" (ma tasnaʿ asnaʿ mithlahu wa-akramuka). And if you wish, "wa-akramuka" (and I honour you) is read as "wa-anā akramuka" (and I honour you). And if you wish, "wa-akramuka" in the jussive (jazman), there is room for consideration, in light of what Sibawayh has recorded in his book. He said: "Know that the accusative after the fa' and the waw in his saying: 'If you come to me, I will come to you and give you'" is weak, and it is of a kind with his saying:

﴿And join with the Hijaz and seek rest﴾ [[The explanation of this line was given earlier in volume one, page 557; refer to it if you wish. — its corrector.]]

This is permissible, but it is neither the proper form of speech nor its correct basis, except that in the conditional it becomes somewhat stronger, since it is not necessary that he does it; unless the earlier clause already involves an act. When it resembles what does not necessarily entail the action, such as the interrogative and the like, they permitted it here despite its weakness, end quote. It is not permissible to take a widely transmitted reading as resting on a weak basis that is neither the proper form of speech nor its correct basis. Had it belonged to this category, Sibawayh would not have left his book free of it, and he mentioned its counterparts among the difficult verses.

If you ask: how does the meaning hold with the jussive "wa-yaʿlama"? I answer: it is as if he said: "or if He wills, He combines three matters: the destruction of one people, the deliverance of another, and the warning of others," (min mahīs) meaning, from evading His punishment.

ما الأولى (*mā al-ūlā*) ضمنت معنى الشرط (*sharṭ*, conditional), فجاءت الفاء في جوابها بخلاف الثانية.

عن على رضى الله عنه: اجتمع لأبى بكر رضى الله عنه مال فتصدق به كله في سبيل الله والخير، فلامه المسلمون وخطأه الكافرون، فنزلت.

And those who avoid the major sins and indecencies (al-kaba'ir al-ithm) — this is coordinated (ʿatf) upon "alladhina amanu" (those who believe), and so is what follows it. The meaning of "kaba'ir al-ithm" is: major sins of this kind. It has also been read as "kabir al-ithm" (the great sin). And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that "kabir al-ithm" is shirk (associating partners with Allah).

"Hum yaghfirun" means: they are the ones especially deserving of forgiveness (al-akhassa' bi'l-ghufran) in a state of anger. Anger does not overpower their forbearance (ahlam) as it overpowers the forbearance of people. The bringing of "hum" (them) and placing it as the subject (mubtada'), and attributing "yaghfirun" to it, is for this benefit. A similar example is:

﴿هُمْ يَنْتَصِرُونَ﴾ (they are the ones who defend themselves).

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 42, verse 38:

﴿And those who respond to their Lord﴾: it was revealed concerning the Ansar. God, mighty and majestic, called them to faith in Him and obedience to Him, and they responded to Him by believing in Him and obeying Him, ﴿and establish the prayer﴾, that is, they completed the five prayers. Before Islam, and before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to Medina, whenever a matter arose among them, they would gather and consult one another, so God praised them, meaning: they do not single out an opinion until they have gathered together upon it. And on the authority of al-Hasan:

"No people have consulted together but they were guided to the most right course of their affair."[[Reported by Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari in al-Adab, and Abd Allah ibn Ahmad in his Zawaid al-Zuhd. The author (al-Zamakhshari) mentioned it as a marfu' narration in Al ʿImran.]] Al-shura (consultation): it is a verbal noun like al-futya, meaning tashawur (mutual consultation). The meaning of His saying ﴿and their affair is by consultation among them﴾ is: possessing consultation (dhu shura), and likewise their saying: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) left the caliphate to shura.

It is that they limit their retaliation to what God has made permissible for them, and do not transgress. It is related from al-Nakha'i (al-Nakha'i) that when he recited it he would say: "They used to dislike humiliating themselves, lest the wicked become emboldened against them." If you ask: Are they praiseworthy for retaliating? I say: Yes, because whoever takes his right without exceeding the limit of God and what He has commanded, and does not commit excess in killing (if he is a guardian of blood), or responds to a foolish person in defense of his honor and as a deterrent to him, then he is obedient.

And every obedient person is praiseworthy.

Both acts: the first (the wrongdoing) and its recompense are evil, because it harms the one upon whom it descends. God the Exalted said: ﴿And if an evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you (O Prophet)."﴾ He means: what harms them of calamities and afflictions. The meaning is that when an offence is returned, it should be requited with its like, without excess. So if someone says, "May God disgrace you," the reply is: "May God disgrace you." ﴿But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation between himself and his adversary, by forgiveness and overlooking, [his reward is with God]﴾, as God said: ﴿Then the one between whom and yourself there was enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend﴾. ﴿His reward is upon God﴾: an indeterminate promise whose greatness cannot be measured. And His saying ﴿Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers﴾ is an indication that in retaliation there is hardly a safeguard against exceeding the bounds of the offence. [[Mahmud said: "In it is an indication that in retaliation there is hardly a safeguard ... etc." Ahmad said: This is a good meaning to answer the one who says: why is this mentioned right after the pardon, when retaliation is not wrongdoing? **Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 42, verse 43:**

﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ The returning pronoun (al-raji') has been omitted because it is understood, as in the saying "the ghee is two manns for a dirham" (al-samn manwan bi-dirham), where the pronoun is also omitted. Khashi'in (humbled), diminished and abased by the disgrace that overtakes them; it may be attached to "from the disgrace" with "they look," and it may be stopped upon at "khashi'in." They look from a faint glance, meaning their gaze begins with a weak, hidden movement of their eyelids, a furtive glance, as you see the one condemned (al-masbur) looking at the sword ["His saying 'as you see the one condemned to the sword' means: the one imprisoned for execution. It was said: they will be gathered blind, so they will not look except with their hearts, and that is a glance from a hidden corner. And this is strained (fihi ta'assuf).

Al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 42, verse 48:

By "man" (al-insan) he means the category, not a single individual, as shown by His words ﴿And if an evil befalls them﴾, when He meant only the criminals, because the befalling of an evil "for what their hands have sent forth" applies only to them. Mercy (al-rahmah) is blessing, such as health, wealth and security. Evil (al-sayyi'ah) is affliction, such as sickness, poverty and fears. "Kafur" (ungrateful) is one who is emphatic in ingratitude (al-kufran). He did not say "fa-innahu kafur" (then he is ungrateful), in order to record that this category is marked by ingratitude for blessings. [[Mahmud said: "He did not say 'fa-innahu kafur' in order to record of this category that it is marked by ingratitude for blessings... etc." Ahmad said: The author overlooked this very point in the verse before it, His words ﴿And those who believe will say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. For the commentary on surah 42, verses 49–50:

When He mentioned that man is given a taste of mercy and is struck by its opposite, He followed this with (the statement) that to Him belongs the dominion, and that He apportions blessing and affliction as He wills, and bestows upon His servants offspring as His will requires: He singles out some with females, some with males, some with both, and renders others barren, so that He grants them no child at all. If you ask: why did He mention the females first, before the males, although the males precede them, and then returned and mentioned the males first? And why did He define the males after having indefinitely named the females?

I say: because He mentioned affliction at the end of the first verse, and man's ingratitude through forgetting the mercy previously granted to him, then followed it with mention of His dominion and His will and the mention of the apportioning of offspring. He put the females first because the context of the speech is that He does what He wills, not what man wills, so mentioning the females, who are among what man does not will, is more important, and the more important must be placed first. And (He mentioned) the females (in this way) because they were the kind that the Arabs regarded as an affliction, and the mention of affliction (came first). He then placed the males later, and when He delayed them for this reason, He made up for their delay, since they deserve to be placed first by virtue of their definiteness, because definiteness is an honouring and a making famous. It is as if He had said: He grants to whomever He wills the famous knights, the well-known ones who are not hidden from you. Then He gave each of the two kinds its due in precedence and posteriority, and made clear that placing the females first was not because of their precedence, but for another requirement, so He said ﴿males and females﴾, as He said ﴿Indeed We created you from a male and a female﴾, and ﴿made from it the two mates, the male and the female﴾.

It has also been said: it was revealed concerning the prophets, may God's blessings and peace be upon them, since He granted Shu'ayb and Lot females, Abraham males, Muhammad (ﷺ) males and females, and rendered Yahya and 'Isa barren. ﴿Indeed He is All-Knowing of the interests of His servants, All-Powerful over bringing into being what benefits them.﴾

It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger, in three ways.

Either by way of wahy (revelation), which is inspiration and casting into the heart, or in a dream, as He revealed to the mother of Musa and to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, concerning the slaughter of his son. And it is related from Mujahid: Allah revealed the Zabur to Dawud, peace be upon him, into his chest.

Ubayd ibn al-Abras said:

"And Allah revealed to me that they have conspired / against the camels of Abu Awfa, so I rose upon one foot."

Meaning: Allah inspired me and cast into my heart that they had conspired. (Here "an" is the lightened form of "anna," and its noun is the pronoun of the people or the matter-and-situation. Abu Hayyan chose that when it is lightened it has no noun, since it is inoperative. If "awha" is taken to include the meaning of "qala" (said), then "an" is explanatory, meaning: they have conspired, of the pattern tafa'alu, that is, they consulted about the matter, or they resolved their affair together. From the same root comes "ya'tamiruna bika liyaqtuluka" (they conspire against you to kill you), and "bi-ibil Abi Awfa" (the camels of Abu Awfa), or "li-yaghtasibuha" (to seize them). So I rose in pursuit of them to return them, "upon a man," meaning I did not wait until I mounted. Or "upon one foot," meaning quickly, so that I did not set both my feet on the ground.)

That is: He inspired me and cast into my heart.

Or by His speaking to him, creating His speech in some bodies, without the hearer seeing who is speaking to him, because He in His essence is not visible. (The phrase "because He in His essence is not visible" means that seeing Him is not permissible; this is the view of the Mu'tazila. As for Ahl al-Sunna, seeing Him is permissible, as established in its proper place. (A))

His words "or from behind a veil" are like: just as a king who is veiled speaks to some of his close companions from behind the curtain, so that his voice is heard and his person is not seen. This is how He spoke to Musa, and how He speaks to the angels.

Or by sending to him a messenger from among the angels, who reveals to him by revelation, as He spoke to the prophets other than Musa. It is said: "wahyan" as He revealed to the messengers through the mediation of angels, "aw yursila rasulan," meaning a prophet, as He speaks to the peoples of the prophets through their tongues. "Wahyan" and "an yursila" are two verbal nouns functioning as circumstantial accusatives (hal), because "an yursila" carries the meaning of "irsalan" (sending). "Min wara'i hijab" is also a circumstantial adverbial phrase, like His words "wa 'ala junubihim" (and upon their sides). The sense is: it is not for any human that Allah speak to him except by revealing, or speaking from behind a veil, or sending. It is also permissible that "wahyan" is placed in the position of "kalaman" (speech), since revelation is hidden speech delivered swiftly, just as you say: "I do not speak to him except openly or in a whisper," since openness and whispering are two kinds of speech. Likewise "irsalan": placing speech on the tongue of a messenger is equivalent to speech without intermediary; you say: "I said such-and-such to so-and-so," though it was in fact said by your agent or your messenger. His words "or from behind a veil" mean: or by causing to hear from behind a veil. As for one who takes "wahyan" to mean "an yuhha" (that He reveal), and conjoins "yursila" to it, the sense is "It is not for any human that Allah speak to him except by revelation," meaning: except by revealing, or by sending. Then one must supply the phrase "or from behind a veil" with a supposition that agrees with both, such as: "or that He cause to hear from behind a veil." (Note: "or that He cause to hear from behind a veil" perhaps should read "or by" (A).)

It has been recited as "aw yursila rasulun fa-yuha" with nominative case, meaning: "or He sends a messenger, and he reveals," or as a predicate meaning "mursilan" conjoined with "wahyan" in the sense of "muhhiyan" (one who reveals).

It is related that the Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Will you not speak to God and look at Him, if you are a prophet, as He spoke to Musa and Musa looked at Him? We will not believe in you until you do that." He said: "Musa did not look at Allah," and this verse was revealed. And it is related from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her: "Whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has greatly slandered Allah." Then she said: "Have you not heard your Lord say: 'Vision does not comprehend Him, but He comprehends vision' (6:103)? and I recited this verse: 'It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation...'" [Agreed upon; part of it was mentioned earlier in al-An'am.]

Then: "Indeed He is Most High above the attributes of created beings, Wise, who conducts His actions according to the requirement of wisdom, so He speaks at times through an intermediary and at other times without one: either by inspiration or by direct address."

Ruḥan min amrinā (a spirit from Our command): He means what was revealed to him, because people are given life through it in their religion, just as the body is given life by the spirit.

If you say: he (ﷺ) knew that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not know the Book before the revelation... [[Maḥmūd said: "If you say: the Prophet (ﷺ) knew that he did not know the Book before the revelation... etc." Aḥmad said: Since al-Zamakhsharī's belief was that faith (īmān) is the name of affirmation (taṣdīq) together with many acts of obedience, both performed and abandoned, so that the monotheist who commits a sin, even a single major one, is not given the name of faith and is not included in the promise to the believers, he noticed that this verse could be used to support his belief, considered it an opportunity to seize and a prize to secure, and was far from presenting the doctrine of the People of the Sunna in the form of a question so that he could answer it according to his own belief.
